pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: src/athena/lane/ports.py:3 The lane is daemon-side Python. It holds no credential, reads no env or config value, reaches no data store and fetches nothing outbound: a search of src/athena/lane and tests/lane for secret, credential, api_key, redact, upstream and fetch found nothing, and 'token' only turned up approval-choice tokens and LLM usage counts. So the question of whether the browser holds a credential is never decided here, and none of the subject's enforcement points exist in this context.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/lane/ports.py:3 No configuration value is read here (no getenv/environ access in the lane), so no value can change side between bundle and server.
src/athena/lane/browser_lane.py:20 The lane holds no executor for host tools and puts no secret on any upstream call. It brokers approvals, not credentials.
src/athena/lane/browser_lane.py:21 Execution happens in the user's browser from their own network position, which is the technique's own named exception. The server-side lane makes no fetch.
src/athena/lane/browser_lane.py:171 There is no upstream broker route. Refusal reasons already come from a closed set, and `detail` carries internal approval/catalog messages, not upstream bodies.
src/athena/lane/ports.py:163 Writes go through injected ports (brain episodes, ledger). No browser-reachable table or row policy exists in this context.
src/athena/lane/ports.py:4 No data-store grants or views. No public role reads any table through this lane.
src/athena/lane/ports.py:7 No schema is defined or reachable here, so structural column omission has nothing to act on.
src/athena/lane/browser_lane.py:231 The streamed events are model turn events going to the user's own panel, not a debug surface over requests that carried other parties' credentials.
